- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts peak too early and then plateau or slightly decline, while true outcomes often show sustained upward momentum or sharp corrections later.
- After a spike in the history (e.g., 74+), model fails to adjust downward quickly — overestimates the peak and underestimates the subsequent decline.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts tend to converge toward a “middle” value, missing the true volatility or trend continuation.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days in the early part of the 30d window, especially when true values are rising sharply.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of corrections after spikes — fails to recognize that prices often drop more than forecasted after a peak.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — lack sharp transitions — while true outcomes show more abrupt changes, especially around mid-to-late window.
- Model tends to overfit recent history, leading to overconfidence in short-term trends, especially when recent values are high.
- When true outcome starts declining after a peak, model continues to forecast upward or flat — fails to anticipate the reversal.
- Model does not account for “rebound” or “reversion to mean” after a sharp spike — often underestimates the correction depth.
